source_title: Spin Master Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results and Reiterates 2026 Full Year Outlook - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
TORONTO , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Spin Master Corp. ("Spin Master" or the "Company") (TSX: TOY) www.spinmaster.com ), a leading global children's entertainment company, today announced its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Company's full Management's Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A") for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ ( www.sedarplus.com ) and posted on the Company's web site at www.spinmaster.com . All financial information is presented in United States dollars ("$", "dollars" and "US$") and has been rounded to the nearest hundred thousand, except per share amounts and where otherwise indicated.
"Our third-quarter results demonstrated steady progress against our 2026 strategic priorities," said Christina Miller, CEO, Spin Master. "I am proud of the collaboration and flawless execution of PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie across our entire company. By fully aligning our creative centers, we expanded our global audience, driving increased viewership across the PAW Patrol content universe and a 25% increase in related toy sales in the quarter. We returned Melissa & Doug to growth through increased shelf space, continued global expansion, and new product innovation. And we took steps toward fully realizing Toca Boca World by successfully bridging digital acquisition and engagement with physical retail and brand partnerships, resulting in an increase in players and double-digit growth in revenue. Our focus remains on driving disciplined, long-term expansion, investing in innovation, entering new categories, and shaping the future of play with acquisitions like Hapiko."
"We have more than doubled operating cash flow in 2026 through disciplined operational execution and working capital management improvements," said Jonathan Roiter, CFO, Spin Master. "This has provided us with resources to reinvest in multiple organic and inorganic growth initiatives across the business, including advanced technology, innovation, and content, while repaying significant debt and returning capital to shareholders through our dividend and active share buyback program."
Consolidated Financial Highlights for Q3 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025
Revenue was stable at $732.7 million, decreasing 0.3%. Constant Currency Revenue1 was $732.0 million, declining 0.4%.
Operating Income was $112.5 million, a decrease of 25.5%.
Adjusted Operating Income 1 was $148.4 million, a decrease of 8.6%.
Net Income was $79.0 million or $0.77 per share (diluted) compared to $106.8 million or $1.03 per share (diluted).
Adjusted Net Income 1 was $106.2 million or $1.03 per share (diluted) compared to $115.2 million or $1.11 per share (diluted).
Adjusted EBITDA 1 was stable at $194.7 million, decreasing by 0.4%
Adjusted EBITDA Margin 1 was 26.6% in both periods.
Cash provided by operating activities was $102.2 million compared to $62.6 million.
Free Cash Flow 1 was $64.9 million compared to $21.6 million.
Repurchased and cancelled 605,757 subordinate voting shares for $8.8 million (C$12.4 million) in Q3 2026 through the Company's Normal Course Issuer Bid. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased and cancelled 212,400 subordinate voting shares for $3.1 million.
On August 26, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the shares of Hapiko Inc., a Brooklyn-based children's technology-related company, for total consideration of $36.2 million.
Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company declared a quarterly dividend of C$0.12 per outstanding subordinate voting share and multiple voting share, payable on January 8, 2027.
1 Non-GAAP financial measure or ratio. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Ratios".
The Company announced that Kate Rouch has been appointed to Spin Master's Board of Directors. A seasoned marketing executive, Ms. Rouch has built global brands at some of the world's most influential technology companies. Most recently she served as OpenAI's first Chief Marketing Officer, building and leading its global marketing organization and has also held leadership positions at Meta and Coinbase . Ms. Rouch is a graduate of Harvard University and has been named one of the world's 10 Most Influential CMOs by Forbes.
For the full year 2026, the Company continues to expect:
Revenue: stable to low single digit percentage growth compared to 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA1: mid to high single digit percentage growth compared to 2025.

Toy Revenue declined by $19.4 million, or 3.0%, to $631.0 million primarily due to lower Toy Gross Product Sales 1 and higher sales allowances. Constant Currency Toy Revenue 1 was $630.1 million, a decrease of 3.1%.
Toy Gross Product Sales1 declined by $15.5 million, or 2.1%, to $727.2 million, primarily driven by lower shipment volumes related to partner licensed brands, partially offset by shipments for the theatrical release of PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie and higher sales of Melissa & Doug . Constant Currency Toy Gross Product Sales 1 was $726.3 million, a decrease of 2.2%.
Sales Allowances increased by $3.5 million to $97.5 million. As a percentage of Toy Gross Product Sales 1 , Sales Allowances increased to 13.4% from 12.7%, primarily driven by changes in geographic and customer mix.
Toys Operating Income decreased by $8.7 million to $120.1 million, primarily driven by lower Toy Revenue and higher marketing expense due to a shift in timing of marketing spend in the Toys segment into the second half of the year, partially offset by lower administrative and selling expenses. Toys Operating Margin was 19.0% compared to 19.8%.
Toys Adjusted EBITDA 1 decreased by $10.4 million, primarily driven by lower Toy Revenue and higher marketing expenses, partially offset by lower administrative and selling expenses.
Toys Adjusted EBITDA Margin 1 was 23.1% compared to 24.0%, primarily driven by lower Toy Revenue resulting in lower operating leverage.

Entertainment Revenue increased by $20.0 million to $52.8 million, primarily driven by distribution revenue from the delivery of the PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie and higher ongoing distribution revenue from the PAW Patrol series.
Entertainment Operating Income declined by $0.6 million to $11.3 million, primarily driven by $11.7 million of impairment for entertainment content development assets, reflecting changes in strategies, partially offset by the delivery of the PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie (distribution revenue less amortization of production costs) and higher ongoing distribution revenue from the PAW Patrol series. Entertainment Operating Margin decreased from 36.3% to 21.4%.
Entertainment Adjusted Operating Income1 increased by $11.1 million to $23.3 million, primarily due to the delivery of PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie in the current year (distribution revenue less amortization of production costs), higher ongoing distribution revenue from the PAW Patrol series, and lower marketing expenses.
Entertainment Adjusted Operating Margin1 increased from 37.2% to 44.1%, primarily due to lower operating expenses, partially offset by the dilutive effect of the delivery of PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie in the current year.

The Company has a committed unsecured revolving credit facility (the "Facility") with a borrowing capacity of $510.0 million and contains certain financial covenants. On May 26, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to amend its existing Facility, which now matures on May 26, 2031. The amendment also introduced an additional three-year revolver tranche with a borrowing capacity of $225.0 million that matures on May 26, 2029. This new tranche was used to settle the $225.0 million non-revolving credit facility ("Acquisition Facility") that was originally entered into on November 20, 2023 to fund the acquisition of Melissa & Doug, which was cancelled on May 26, 2026.
As at September 30, 2026, there was $163.0 million outstanding (December 31, 2025 - $42.0 million) under the Facility. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company drew $137.0 million (2025 - $25.0 million) on the Facility, and repaid $241.0 million (2025 - $30.0 million) against the Facility. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the weighted average interest rates on the Facility was 5.1% (2025 - 5.7%).
As at September 30, 2026, the Company had available liquidity of $635.0 million, comprised of $47.5 million in cash and $587.5 million under the Company's committed credit facilities.
Cash Flows for Q3 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025
Cash flows provided by operating activities were $102.2 million compared to $62.6 million driven by change in changes in non-cash working capital. Changes in non-cash working capital decreased by $81.3 million as compared to a decrease of $119.9 million.
Cash used in investing activities was $70.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $42.7 million primarily as a result of the acquisition of Hapiko and higher investments in computer software, partially offset by lower investments in leasehold improvements, equipment, intellectual property and Entertainment content development.
Cash flows used in financing activities were $32.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $19.2 million, driven by repayment of $94.6 million towards loans and borrowings (2025 - $nil), lease payments of $8.1 million (2025-$2.5 million), partially offset by $87.0 million drawn from loans and borrowings (2025 - $nil).
Free Cash Flow 1 was $64.9 million compared to $21.6 million, primarily due to changes in non-cash working capital.
1 Non-GAAP financial measure or ratio. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Ratios".
The Company's Board of Directors declared a dividend of C$0.12 per outstanding subordinate voting share and multiple voting share, payable on January 8, 2027 to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 24, 2026. The dividend is designated to be an eligible dividend for purposes of section 89(1) of the Income Tax Act (Canada).
